facts.raw_span: a history of biopsy-proven psoriasis
juvenile dermatomyositis (DM)
her juvenile DM had been in remission for several years
previous treatments included adalimumab, etanercept, methotrexate, guselkumab, ustekinumab, and topical corticosteroids
fatigue
difficulty picking up her child, and climbing stairs
Diffuse ill-defined erythema and mild edema of the face and eyelids
Violaceous to erythematous patches on the joints, periungual skin, and chest
Scaly erythematous plaques on lateral leg
Photodistributed poikiloderma on chest
Creatine kinase levels: normal
Aldolase levels: normal

concepts.why: The patient has a history of biopsy-proven psoriasis and presents with scaly erythematous plaques on the lateral leg.
The patient has a history of juvenile dermatomyositis and presents with violaceous to erythematous patches on the joints, periungual skin, and chest.
The patient has a history of psoriasis and presents with joint involvement, suggesting a possible diagnosis of psoriatic arthritis.
The patient presents with diffuse ill-defined erythema, photodistributed poikiloderma, and other skin findings that could be consistent with systemic lupus erythematosus.
The patient has a history of juvenile dermatomyositis and presents with a combination of skin and joint findings that could be consistent with mixed connective tissue disease.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's history of juvenile dermatomyositis, violaceous to erythematous patches on the joints, and previous remission with treatment suggest dermatomyositis as the primary condition, despite current normal creatine kinase levels.
